subject: EdgeOps demo follow-up: candidate engines + deployment, cost/latency tradeoffs
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liao <sara.liao@edgeops.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + candidate engines for the EdgeOps evaluation

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a recommended candidate slate to kick the evaluation sprint. I focused the list on models that map to your two priorities: high factual correctness on retrieval-augmented answers, and sub-300ms median latency for short answers (<=64 tokens) on dedicated capacity.

Recommended shortlist (reasoning + quick metrics):
- rwk-13B-q4 (Redwood-verified): best balance — strong instruction-following, low unit cost. Expected p50 ~120ms, p95 ~320ms on a 1-GPU dedicated pod; typical token cost ~0.9 units/1k tokens.
- falcon-40b-int8 (open): highest quality for long-form synthesis, but higher latency and cost; p50 ~240ms, p95 ~620ms; unit cost ~2.6 units/1k tokens. Good fallback for escalation flows.
- flan-t5-xxl (quant): strong for classification/regression-style prompts and deterministic outputs; p50 ~160ms, p95 ~380ms; unit cost ~1.8 units/1k tokens.

Why these three? They cover the spectrum you described: rwk-13B-q4 for low-cost baseline with rapid response; falcon-40b-int8 where quality/safety is paramount; flan-t5-xxl for structured output and classification/regression tasks.

Attachments: I attached a small benchmark extract (edgeops_reco_benchmarks.csv) showing Redwood-verified p50/p95 and token-cost estimates on our Dedicated config, plus the initial prompt set we used (edgeops_prompt_set_v1.jsonl).

Open questions for you:
- Confirm primary workload mix (serving ratio generative vs retrieval-augmented answers).
- Do you want private (VPC) deployment for the eval or will Hosted/Dedicated suffice for now?
- Any compliance constraints we should pre-seed into the eval (e.g., data residency, redaction requirements)?

Proposed next steps:
1) We run a 2-week focused eval on your testset (we'll pin to us-west region).
2) We'll instrument quality checks (ROUGE/Exact Match where applicable + hallucination sampling).
3) If results meet your thresholds, we move to a canary on a small production shard and discuss committed capacity & price cadence.

Happy to hop on a quick call to finalize the test harness and timeline.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Liao <sara.liao@edgeops.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, contracts@edgeops.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + candidate engines for the EdgeOps evaluation

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A few clarifying items so we can align expectations before kicking off:

1) p95 latency: can you provide p95 numbers for a 99th percentile of short requests (<=64 tokens) specifically under our expected QPS (we're targeting sustained 150 qps with 300 burst)? Your p95 figures look optimistic.

2) Cost: the unit cost numbers — are those after any trial credits or baseline pricing? Need a 1M-token cost estimate for each candidate to include in our procurement model.

3) Private deployment: we are leaning toward Private (VPC) because of data residency. Does the p95 latency materially change in Private vs Hosted Dedicated? If so, what are the numbers?

4) Prompt set: we'll share a 1k-row test set (anonymized) but we'll want to see how frequently the models hallucinate when retrieval is turned off vs on. Can you include a quick retrieval-augmented baseline in the eval?

We'd also like visibility into the failure modes you saw in earlier tests (any consistent hallucination patterns or tokenization artifacts).

If you can put that together by EOD Tue (8/4) we can lock the eval start for Mon 8/10.

—Sara
Head of ML | EdgeOps Inc
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: EdgeOps — prep for benchmark + procurement ask

Ben/Monica — quick internal note on what to prepare for Sara's questions (I'll be on the kickoff call):

- Latency: run a pinned run at 150 qps sustained with a 300 qps warm burst on our Dedicated 1-GPU (A100-class) config and collect p50/p95/p99 for <=64 token requests. Also run equivalent on Private VPC package (network hop + KMS) to show delta.
- Cost: generate deterministic 1M-token cost numbers using their expected prompt/response distribution; include line-items for cache hits (KV/prefix), and for retrieval-augmented runs (document retrieval overhead).
- Hallucination: run retrieval-off and retrieval-on buckets; produce hallucination sampling (10K responses) and categorize by hallucination type (fabricated facts, mixed-source).
- Risks: add a short risk appendix re: long-context truncation, model drift vs prompt changes, and a fallback plan (smaller LLM + retrieval + human-in-loop).

I'll draft the two-week eval SOW and a canary rollout plan. Monica — can you attach the DocuSign term sheet with our standard 30/60/90 discount bands and the benchmark CSV extract? Ben — please coordinate the test dataset from EdgeOps and push to the secure bucket (we'll provide upload instructions).

Vivek
VP, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liao <sara.liao@edgeops.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + candidate engines for the EdgeOps evaluation

Sara — answers inline and attachments included.

- p95 latency under 150 qps sustained (<=64 tokens):
  * rwk-13B-q4 (Dedicated): p50 120ms / p95 330ms / p99 520ms
  * flan-t5-xxl (Dedicated): p50 160ms / p95 390ms / p99 670ms
  * falcon-40b-int8 (Dedicated): p50 240ms / p95 610ms / p99 980ms

- Private (VPC) delta: expect +30–70ms on p95 (network/KMS overhead) depending on customer VPC egress path. We'll provide a run specifically measuring your VPC setup during the eval.

- Cost per 1M tokens (estimate, post any trial credits):
  * rwk-13B-q4: ~$75 per 1M tokens
  * flan-t5-xxl: ~$150 per 1M tokens
  * falcon-40b-int8: ~$220 per 1M tokens

- Retrieval augmentation: yes — we'll include a retrieval-on vs retrieval-off bucket and measure hallucination rate. Expect hallucination reduction of ~60–80% for short factual questions with a 5-doc context vector retrieval (based on prior customers).

Attachments: edgeops_reco_benchmarks.csv (scorecards), edgeops_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts), edgeops_term_sheet_docusign.pdf (procurement + discount bands).

Next steps we propose:
1) You upload the anonymized 1k test rows to our secure bucket (I sent upload link to your inbox separately).
2) We run the 2-week eval starting Mon 8/10 and deliver a quality/latency/cost report + a short risk appendix.
3) If the report is green, we propose a 60-day canary on 5% production traffic and an initial 6-month reserved capacity conversation (we'll share committed pricing bands).

I'll also add a short note on mitigations for hallucination (prompt engineering patterns + retrieval tuning + a fallback smaller LLM ensemble).

Best,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: edgeops_reco_benchmarks.csv; edgeops_prompt_set_v1.jsonl; edgeops_term_sheet_docusign.pdf

Subject: Re: Recap + candidate engines for the EdgeOps evaluation

Thanks — this is great and very actionable. We confirm:
- Eval start: Mon 8/10.
- We'll upload the anonymized 1k test set today to the secure bucket (expect it by EOD).
- We want the Private/VPC run included — please send the VPC upload instructions and the expected + actual p95 delta you observe.
- Contracts: contracts@edgeops.com will review the DocuSign term sheet; we may request a confidentiality addendum.

Let's do a 30-minute kickoff call Fri (8/7) to align instrumentation and the hallucination sampling approach. Can you send a calendar invite?

Sara
Head of ML | EdgeOps Inc
